deepfake-threat.title: Lead with the deepfake threat
deepfake-threat.what: The homepage and launches put AI fraud front and center. Deepsight is pitched as protection from deepfakes, injected virtual cameras and synthetic identities, with each check running in under 100 milliseconds.
deepfake-threat.metric: Under 100 ms per check · claimed 10x more accurate than trained human reviewers (internal tests)
deepfake-threat.take: Fear of a new, fast-growing threat opens doors that a pitch about better onboarding never would. The buyer's old vendor now looks like it was built for yesterday's fraud.

deepfake-guesser.title: Deepfake Guesser Challenge at the booth
deepfake-guesser.what: At Money20/20 Europe the booth runs a game: visitors try to tell real faces from deepfakes. The event page pairs it with a talk on fighting deepfakes and a form to request a meeting.
deepfake-guesser.metric: Booth #1C150 · request-a-meeting form on the event page
deepfake-guesser.take: A fraud lead who fails to spot a fake has felt the pain in person. The meeting request right after the game catches them while that feeling is fresh.

own-events.title: Own event series: Decoded
own-events.what: Besides big booths at Money20/20 USA and Europe, Incode hosts its own invite-style event, Decoded: Fraud & Identity in Focus (London, November 2025), promoted on the homepage.
own-events.metric: Money20/20 USA booth #11047 · Decoded London, 18 Nov 2025
own-events.take: Owning the room means Incode sets the agenda and the guest list. Senior fraud and risk leaders meet peers, and Incode is the host of that conversation.

agentic-identity.title: Name the next problem: Agentic Identity
agentic-identity.what: Incode launched Agentic Identity to verify, authorize and monitor autonomous AI agents. Every agent is linked to a verified human owner, with consent and scope controls and live behavior tracking. Pilots started in Q4 2025.
agentic-identity.take: Naming a problem before buyers have budget for it makes Incode the reference point when that budget appears. It also supports the 'vision' axis analysts score.

ai-info-page.title: A fact sheet written for AI assistants
ai-info-page.what: A dedicated AI info page lists the company facts in plain, quotable form: 700+ enterprise clients, 4.1B+ trust checks a year, 400M+ identity profiles, about 4 seconds average verification, 98% validated on the first try.
ai-info-page.metric: 700+ enterprise clients · 4.1B+ trust checks a year
ai-info-page.take: Buyers now ask ChatGPT or Google AI to shortlist vendors. A clean fact page shapes what those answers say about Incode before a human ever visits the site.

latam-roots.title: Local sites and logos for Latin America
latam-roots.what: Spanish and Portuguese versions of the site, plus a logo set heavy with Latin American leaders: Nu, Banorte, Citibanamex, Rappi, Davivienda.
latam-roots.take: In markets where global vendors often feel distant, local language and familiar local banks signal that Incode understands the regulators and the fraud patterns there.

industry-pages.title: Industry pages in the buyer's own language
industry-pages.what: Separate pages for financial services, telco, gaming, marketplaces and government. Each speaks to that industry's fraud and rules, with its own headline numbers. The telco page, for example, claims 99% fraud reduction and 40% higher conversion.
industry-pages.take: A telco fraud lead reading about SIM-swap and account takeover feels understood. One generic identity pitch would force them to translate it for their own world.

two-budgets.title: Less fraud and more sign-ups at once
two-budgets.what: The pitch refuses the usual trade-off between security and friction. Fraud numbers (0.01% false acceptance) sit next to growth numbers (98% pass on the first try, 20% conversion uplift when checking against government records).
two-budgets.take: Fraud teams want fewer bad users; growth teams want fewer dropped good ones. Selling both outcomes lets the deal draw on two budgets and wins two internal allies.

fraud-reports.title: State of Identity Fraud webinars
fraud-reports.what: Webinars and reports such as the 2025 State of Identity Fraud bring together industry experts on new fraud techniques and how to stop them. The AuthenticID content library now runs under the Incode banner.
fraud-reports.take: Teaching the fraud team what attackers do next makes Incode a trusted advisor. Each lesson ends with the capability that answers the threat.

dev-hub.title: Open developer hub
dev-hub.what: Public docs for the Omni platform explain setup, credentials, SDKs and APIs. Engineers can judge how hard integration will be before they ever talk to sales.
dev-hub.take: Engineers often hold a quiet veto. Letting them evaluate on their own turns them from a blocker into a supporter, and shows Incode is serious about integration.

logo-wall.title: Logo wall stated as market share
logo-wall.what: Customers are framed as rankings: 8 of the top 10 US banks, 8 of the top 9 US telcos, 3 of the top 3 global neobanks, 4 of the top 5 global marketplaces. Logos across the site include Citi, Wells Fargo, HSBC, Scotiabank, Chime, Nu, Klarna, Binance, TikTok, AT&T, US Cellular, FanDuel, BetMGM, PokerStars and Liga MX.
logo-wall.metric: 8 of top 10 US banks · 8 of top 9 US telcos · 3 of 3 top neobanks · 4 of top 5 marketplaces
logo-wall.take: '8 of the top 10' says 'your peers already chose us' more strongly than any single logo. For a risk-averse bank, the safe choice is the one its competitors made.

gartner-mq.title: Gartner Leader three years running
gartner-mq.what: Incode has been a Leader in every edition of the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Identity Verification: 2024 (the first one), 2025 and 2026. Incode points out that in 2025 only 5 of 11 vendors were named Leaders. The homepage card shows the Magic Quadrant chart itself and offers a 'Download the report' button.
gartner-mq.metric: Leader 2024 · 2025 · 2026 · 5 of 11 vendors were Leaders in 2025
gartner-mq.take: Enterprise procurement starts its shortlist from the Magic Quadrant. Being a Leader every year keeps Incode on every list and gives the champion a safe answer to 'why them?'

ibeta-level3.title: First to pass iBeta Level 3 on iOS and Android
ibeta-level3.what: The independent lab iBeta announced Incode as the first to pass Level 3 presentation attack (liveness) testing under ISO/IEC 30107-3 on both platforms, in early 2026. Incode reports 0% error rates at that level.
ibeta-level3.take: 'First' is a claim a rival can't copy. A lab certificate answers the security team's toughest question with someone else's signature.

g2-badges.title: A haul of G2 badges, announced on the blog
g2-badges.what: Each season's G2 results become a blog post. Summer 2026: 20 badges, 14 in Identity Verification, 3 in Age Verification and 3 in Anti-Money Laundering.
g2-badges.take: Gartner speaks to executives; G2 speaks to the practitioners who use the tool daily. Together they cover both voices in the buying group.

scale-numbers.title: Scale as a moat
scale-numbers.what: Incode repeats its volume everywhere: over 4 billion identity checks a year (together with AuthenticID in 2024), 400M+ identity profiles, 700+ enterprise clients, 600+ staff.
scale-numbers.metric: 4.1B+ trust checks a year · 400M+ identity profiles
scale-numbers.take: In fraud, more data trains better models and spots repeat attackers across customers. The size itself becomes the argument that a smaller vendor can't match.

deepsight-proof.title: University test plus live deployments for Deepsight
deepsight-proof.what: Deepsight claims are backed by an independent Purdue University evaluation and by named deployments at TikTok, Scotiabank and Nubank.
deepsight-proof.metric: Purdue University evaluation · live at TikTok, Scotiabank, Nubank
deepsight-proof.take: A new product has no track record. Borrowing a university's credibility and three famous users fills that gap fast.

government-refs.title: Government references: DMVs and DOTs
government-refs.what: Public-sector customers such as the California DMV and Wisconsin DOT sit alongside the banks.
government-refs.take: If a state trusts Incode with driver identity, a bank's risk committee has less to worry about. Government logos also open other public-sector deals.

sales-led.title: No price list, only a conversation
sales-led.what: There is no public price and no free plan. A blue 'Request a demo' button sits in the top navigation on every page, and pricing is custom, so every serious buyer has to talk to a rep.
sales-led.metric: 'Request a demo' on every page · custom pricing · no free plan
sales-led.take: Price depends on volume, countries and modules, so a quote needs a conversation. That talk is where the rep qualifies the deal and finds the economic buyer.

demo-env.title: Time-boxed demo environment
demo-env.what: New prospects get a shared demo environment with full Omni API access for testing without a production commitment. Access comes through a rep, and evaluation periods are time-limited.
demo-env.take: Full access lets engineers prove it works; the time limit keeps the deal moving. Because access runs through a rep, sales always knows who is testing.

compliance-close.title: Compliance as a closing argument
compliance-close.what: Messaging stresses 'streamlining compliance' for KYC, AML and age verification rules. Badges in AML and Age Verification back it up.
compliance-close.metric: G2 badges in AML and Age Verification
compliance-close.take: A fine is a cost the board understands. When a deadline or regulator is involved, the purchase stops being optional and the timeline speeds up.

iam-plugins.title: Plugs into Okta, Entra, Ping and ServiceNow
iam-plugins.what: Incode Workforce connects to the identity tools companies already run: Okta, Microsoft Entra, Ping Identity and ServiceNow. Incode says setup typically takes less than an hour.
iam-plugins.metric: Setup in under an hour (Incode's claim)
iam-plugins.take: The IT team's main objection is effort. Fitting into tools they already own makes the yes cheap.

lifecycle-expand.title: Land on onboarding, expand across the identity lifecycle
lifecycle-expand.what: A 'Verify identity from every angle' section lists the modules: document verification (4.9K+ ID types in 190+ countries), biometric liveness, government record matching (state DMVs), KYC and AML screening (PEP and sanctions), business verification (KYB) and deepfake detection, for users, businesses and AI agents. A customer that starts with onboarding can switch on the next module without a new vendor.
lifecycle-expand.take: The first module puts the face template and the integration in place. Each later module reuses both, so adding it is far easier than buying from someone else.

workforce-crosssell.title: Workforce: the same tech sold to the CISO
workforce-crosssell.what: Incode Workforce verifies the real person at risky moments inside a company: job interviews, new-hire onboarding, help-desk and MFA resets. It is offered jointly with Okta Workforce Identity.
workforce-crosssell.take: A bank that uses Incode for customers has a security team fighting fake job candidates and help-desk scams. Same account, new buyer, new budget.

acquisitions.title: Buying rivals and their customers
acquisitions.what: Incode bought AuthenticID (August 2025), strong in regulated, high-volume deployments, and later Identiq for privacy-first fraud prevention. AuthenticID's site now carries an 'Incode' banner.
acquisitions.take: Each deal removes a competitor, adds a customer base to cross-sell the full platform into, and fills a product gap without years of building.

recognitions.title: Three analysts, one 'flagship recognitions' row
recognitions.what: A 'Built on trust' section puts three charts side by side: Leader in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for Identity Verification (third year running), Leading Vendor in Liminal's Link Index for KYC, and top-rated in G2's Index for Identity Verification. Each card shows the actual chart with Incode's dot, plus a 'Download the report' or 'Learn more' button.
recognitions.metric: Gartner Leader · Liminal Link Index Leading Vendor · G2 top-rated
recognitions.take: One analyst can be dismissed as a fluke; three different ones agreeing reads as consensus. Showing the real charts lets the buyer see the position for themselves, and the gated report download captures the lead.

release-notes.title: Public release notes every two weeks
release-notes.what: The developer hub publishes detailed platform release notes on a two-week rhythm (Oct 19, Oct 5, Sep 21, Sep 7…), tagged HOTFIX or UPDATE, plus separate notes for Web, iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter, Cordova and Xamarin SDKs, an SDK deprecation policy and an 'Ask AI' assistant over the docs.
release-notes.metric: New release notes every ~2 weeks · 7 SDKs covered
release-notes.take: Engineers judge a vendor by how it ships. Steady, specific fixes (down to Ontario health-card barcodes) prove the product is alive and maintained, which quietly answers 'will they still support this in three years?'

case-studies.title: Case studies: 'Real customers, measurable results'
case-studies.what: A case studies page pairs the headline 'Real customers, measurable results' with a moving wall of logos (Liga MX, Citi, PokerStars, FanDuel, Wells Fargo, Klarna, BetMGM, Citibanamex, US Cellular, Lemon, Binance), then a 'Results from every industry' grid of stories.
case-studies.metric: Stories sorted by industry · results promised up front
case-studies.take: Sorting stories by industry lets each buyer find a twin of their own company. 'Measurable results' sets the expectation that the proof is numbers, not praise.

blog-guides.title: Blog guides that rank: 'Deepfakes 101'
blog-guides.what: Long, search-friendly explainers such as 'Deepfakes 101: Examples and deepfake fraud prevention tips' (9 min read). The table of contents walks the reader from what deepfakes are, their types and famous examples, to why they are dangerous, how to spot them and how to prevent deepfake fraud. A 'Request a demo' button stays in the top bar, and share buttons make it easy to pass along.
blog-guides.metric: 9 min read · 9-step table of contents · demo button on every article
blog-guides.take: People search 'what is a deepfake' long before they search for a vendor. The guide answers that question, builds the fear step by step, and ends on prevention, where Incode's product is the obvious next step. Share buttons let the reader spread it to colleagues for free.
